title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
excerpt: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corrupted or transformed image, generate a restored or canonical image, and interpret the result. The…

ai.summary: ThinkMorph‑SSL is a two‑stage self‑supervised training recipe that uses images themselves as supervision to teach models interleaved multimodal reasoning, eliminating the need for task‑specific demonstration data.
ai.why: Provides a scalable way to build multimodal reasoning models without costly annotation pipelines.

title: PhyCoVE: Benchmarking Physical Counterfactual Video Editing across Diverse Material Dynamics
excerpt: Physical counterfactual video editing turns a source video and a language-specified physical edit at a given execution frame into a counterfactual video that shows how the scene would evolve after the edit. Existing evaluations with counterfactual target videos mainly cover object removal or specific rigid-body motions, although real scenes also involve elastic deformation, fluid flow, and interactions among rigid bodies, elastic solids, and fluids. We introduce PhyCoVE, a benchmark of 533 cases on 110 source videos that covers rigid, elastic, and fluid dynamics in five interaction patterns, with edits that remove an object, change a physical quantity, or insert a new object. For the…

ai.summary: PhyCoVE is a benchmark of 533 cases for physical counterfactual video editing, testing how well models can simulate scene evolution after language-specified edits involving fluids, elastic deformation, and rigid-body interactions.
ai.why: Offers a rigorous evaluation metric for video generation models' understanding of complex physical dynamics, moving beyond simple object removal.

title: ACAP: Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control
excerpt: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between…

ai.summary: ACAP (Asynchronous Coding Agents for Efficient Robot Control) structures a robot as a team of persistent agents, each handling a specific control group (e.g., arm, torso) to enable parallel reasoning and execution.
ai.why: Allows robotics developers to scale control complexity by decoupling subsystems, reducing latency in multi‑component robots.

title: S-Mind: Internalizing Multi-View Geometry for Spatial Intelligence
excerpt: Spatial intelligence, the ability to reason about 3D space from visual observations, becomes essential as multimodal large language models (MLLMs) move into the physical world. Beyond perceiving each view, it rests on two cornerstones of human cognition: fusing multiple views into one coherent 3D scene and mentally transforming that scene to new viewpoints as reasoning unfolds. Yet our spatial probes reveal that MLLMs largely lack both capabilities, even after spatial fine-tuning. We therefore present S-Mind, which internalizes multi-view geometry within the MLLM through a compact set of spatial tokens. It supervises these tokens to hold the fused 3D scene and re-emits them to re-express…

ai.summary: S‑Mind proposes a method for multimodal large language models to internalize multi‑view geometry, enabling 3D scene fusion and viewpoint transformation, which current MLLMs lack even after fine‑tuning.
ai.why: Could enable developers to build LLM‑powered applications that understand and manipulate 3D environments.

title: KMed-31B Technical Report
excerpt: We present KMed-31B, a medical large language model post-trained from an open-weight model for on-premises deployment with limited hardware. Post-training a model for diverse medical tasks remains difficult, because improving one kind of task can lower performance on another. We attribute this to differences between tasks in expected output and available feedback. Medical question answering and diagnosis prediction have reference answers, whereas clinical inquiry has no single correct response and is judged with rubrics. We therefore divide medical training tasks into four categories by these two properties, train one specialist per category with a reward that its feedback supports, and…

ai.summary: KMed‑31B is a 31‑billion‑parameter medical large language model fine‑tuned for on‑premises use, aiming to balance performance across medical QA, diagnosis prediction, and open‑ended clinical inquiry tasks.

title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
excerpt: Computer-use agents (CUAs) built on vision-language models are increasingly entrusted with long-horizon tasks in live desktop, web, and mobile environments, where the screen keeps changing on its own. However, current CUAs lack real-time situational awareness: they perceive the environment through discrete snapshots, and the substantial inference latency of VLMs, compounded by highly dynamic interfaces, opens a perception-action gap in which the observed state frequently becomes stale before the corresponding action is executed. To bridge this gap, we present NightWatch, a plug-and-play framework that endows any CUA with continuous, temporally grounded perception without changing the…

ai.summary: The authors propose a proactive perception framework for computer‑use agents that continuously monitors screen changes instead of relying on discrete snapshots, reducing the perception‑action gap caused by VLM latency.

title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
excerpt: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface. We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration…

ai.summary: ICLWorld is a new online benchmark that evaluates the in-context learning capabilities of agents operating in both digital and physical (robotic) environments, addressing gaps in existing offline or text-only evaluations.
ai.why: Provides a standardized way to measure how well agents adapt to new rules in real-time, which is critical for deploying flexible robotic and digital agents.

title: Qwen-Image-HD: Autoregressive Diffusion for High Definition Image Generation
excerpt: Fine-tuning a generator on a complete high-resolution canvas requires long image sequences and substantial computation, yet local regions can still exhibit unnatural repetitive stripes when training resources are limited. We introduce Qwen-Image-HD, which adapts Qwen-Image 2.0 to high-resolution synthesis through local training and blockwise autoregressive generation. Each prediction covers a target tile at 1K scale, conditioned on high-resolution upper and left neighbors and a compressed historical thumbnail. ai.summary: Qwen‑Image‑HD adapts the Qwen‑Image 2.0 model for high‑definition (≈1K) image generation using blockwise autoregressive diffusion and local training to reduce artifacts and compute cost.

title: Rewirable Circuits in Transformers with Loom Attention
excerpt: We propose loom attention, which allows a Transformer to dynamically rewire its circuits at every token by interweaving a head's vertical attention over the outputs of earlier heads (to obtain its query, key and value) with its horizontal attention over tokens. We instantiate vertical attention efficiently with normalized and gated linear attention over a per-token matrix memory, which stores the compressed head outputs and serves as a second residual stream. This yields LoomFormer, a dual-stream architecture that splits control and content between the vector and matrix streams. Across model sizes and training token budgets in language modeling and downstream tasks, LoomFormer matches…

ai.summary: The paper introduces Loom Attention, which adds a vertical attention stream over earlier head outputs to a transformer’s horizontal token attention, resulting in the dual‑stream LoomFormer architecture.

title: PartAgent: Agentic 3D Part Segmentation via Expert Integration and Closed-Loop Refinement
excerpt: Segmenting a 3D object into semantically meaningful parts requires joint reasoning about geometric structure and semantic context. Pretrained 3D experts provide spatially grounded region proposals, while 2D experts provide semantic cues for identifying object parts. We present PartAgent, a training-free agentic framework for 3D part segmentation built upon two complementary modules: (i) Structural-Semantic Expert Integration combines regions predicted by the 3D expert with multiview semantic evidence from the 2D expert through…

title: Reinforcing Diffusion Models by Instantaneous Trajectory Distribution Matching
excerpt: Forward diffusion reinforcement learning (RL)---enabling deterministic ODE sampling without trajectory backpropagation---has grown increasingly popular for efficiently aligning diffusion models. However, we reveal that existing methods essentially rely on signed reward-weighted regression (RWR), regressing the trainable policy velocity onto rollouts from a behavior distribution. Unbiased baseline subtraction implicitly assumes that the policy velocity equals the behavior marginal velocity---an idealized assumption violated under classifier-free guidance (CFG) rollouts, offline/off-policy updates, and imperfect online self-consistency. ai.summary: The authors show that existing forward‑diffusion reinforcement learning methods implicitly perform signed reward‑weighted regression and propose a corrected approach for unbiased trajectory distribution matching.

excerpt: Computer-use agents (CUAs) are rapidly improving, yet their evaluation remains largely static. title: CoT-Proxy: Cross-Format Transfer for Distilling Long-Horizon Policies
excerpt: Reasoning models become long-horizon agents through reinforcement learning or, more cheaply, through fine-tuning on a stronger teacher's trajectories, which contain the teacher's chain-of-thought as well as its actions. The standard fine-tuning approach imitates both, yet the strongest teachers are closed models whose chain-of-thought is hidden behind an API. We show that the chain-of-thought can be left out altogether and that the long-horizon policy can be distilled from the teacher's actions alone. title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
excerpt: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps…

ai.summary: The paper presents a reinforcement‑learning method that trains agents to commit answers only when their internal belief state is sufficiently certain, using verifiable belief signals during training.
